assessment.most_likely_root_cause: Render Free web-service idle spin-down followed by cold-start/wake latency; the intended GitHub keepalive had no run records and therefore did not establish continuous traffic.
assessment.reasoning: The service is on Render's free plan. Its app logs stop at 2026-10-20T22:36:15.511599725Z; the only current instance was created at 23:35:28Z, about 59 minutes later, and its process completed startup at 23:36:10Z. The known 503 is approximate at 23:37Z, near the documented roughly one-minute free-service wake period. The app then logged 54 generic requests with outcome=success through 23:39:59Z. No app error, failed deploy, or deployment event is present around the incident. This pattern strongly favors a cold-start/platform availability response over an application health-handler failure. However, no request log or timestamped 503 body ties the exact 503 to the wake window, so a transient Render ingress/routing failure is not excluded.
not_claimed: A successful warm retry is not evidence that the cold-start request succeeded.
The exact source of the 503 (Render wake page/router versus another transient platform response) is not proven.
No owner approval, service upgrade, restart, resume, deploy, dispatch, alias change, or budget change was performed.

free_tier_cold_start.assessment: strongly supported; exact 503 source not proven
support: No app logs for about 59 minutes before a new instance was created at 23:35:28Z.
The app completed startup at 23:36:10Z, near the approximate 23:37Z failure and within Render's documented wake interval.
The keepalive workflow has zero run records, so it cannot be credited with keeping this service warm.

render_wide_or_regional_outage.assessment: not supported by the available status snapshot, not excluded
support: Render public status said All Systems Operational at 22:23:43Z, but that is about 73 minutes before the failure.
A GitLab deployment issue was listed, but no runtime availability incident was listed in that snapshot.
No Render request logs or same-time public status snapshot establish whether a transient edge/service outage occurred at 23:37Z.

deployment_crash.assessment: unlikely based on observed deployment history
support: No deploy or build event newer than 2026-09-28 appears in the returned Render history.
The latest deploy remains live and was successfully completed on 2026-09-28.
Render auto-deploy is disabled; the October main-branch merges did not automatically deploy this service.
The new instance logged startup complete and subsequent generic success outcomes; no incident-window app error or failed-deploy record was returned.
The deployed /health/live handler directly returns status ok and performs no readiness/dependency checks.
There are no incident-window application outcome=error entries, although the app log does not identify request paths.
Render lists api.knicksiq.win as verified and associated with the same service.
The provider onrender.com hostname also returned 503, so the failure is not isolated to the custom hostname.
There are no request logs with host/path/status to distinguish common ingress routing from service wake.

keepalive_no_run_diagnosis.established: No workflow run or schedule-run record existed by 2026-10-20T23:41:07Z despite active workflow state, default branch main, repository Actions enabled, and the schedule source on main.
keepalive_no_run_diagnosis.reason_not_established: The queried GitHub REST APIs expose workflow state and runs but returned no scheduler-delivery explanation. The exact reason no run was enqueued remains unknown; do not infer a cron parse error, permission failure, or scheduler outage from the empty run list alone.
keepalive_no_run_diagnosis.production_effect: No keepalive request can be attributed to this workflow during the observed idle gap.

remaining_unknowns: The exact timestamp, response headers, and body of each 503 were not retained in the task-provided signal.
Render emitted zero HTTP request log records in the incident window, so the original 503 cannot be correlated to a host, route, instance, or response generator.
The generic aggregate.request middleware entries do not include paths and cannot prove that /health/live itself succeeded at a given timestamp.
No Render runtime shutdown/spindown event is returned by the queried event history; a free-tier idle spin-down is inferred from plan, quiet logs, and instance creation timing.
The public Render status snapshot was stale relative to the 503 and cannot exclude a transient/regional incident after 22:23Z.
GitHub REST run-list APIs do not explain why the active scheduled workflow generated zero runs.
minimal_next_action: Have the repository owner inspect GitHub Actions scheduler/event-delivery diagnostics for workflow 391089567 (read-only) to learn why scheduled runs were not enqueued. Do not dispatch, edit workflow/default-branch settings, or alter Render service state as part of this diagnosis. If an owner later authorizes one manual dispatch, treat its result only as workflow execution evidence; because it pings the live API, it would warm the service and would not prove cold-start behavior.
